questions.markdown:
A specimen of steel 20 mm diameter with a gauge length of 200 mm is tested to destruction. It has an extension of 0.25 mm under a load of 80 kN and the load at elastic limit is 102 kN. The ultimate load is 130 kN.

The total extension at fracture is 56 mm and diameter at neck is 15 mm. Find
(i) The stress at elastic limit. (ii) Young's modulus. (iii) Percentage elongation. (iv) Percentage reduction in area. (v) Ultimate tensile stress.

A circular rod of 25 mm diameter and 500 mm long is subjected to a tensile force of 60 kN. Determine modulus of rigidity, bulk modulus and change in volume if Poisson's ratio = 0.3 and Young's modulus $E = 2 \times 10^5$ N/mm$^2$.
Draw and explain stress vs strain curve of mild steel of tension test.

With the help of neat sketches, define the following terms:

i) Moment of Inertia ii) Radius of gyration.

A compound bar of length 600 mm consists of a strip of aluminium 40 mm wide and 20 mm thick and a strip of steel 60 mm wide $\times$ 15 mm thick rigidly joined at the ends. If elastic modulus of aluminium and steel are $1 \times 10^5$ N/mm$^2$ and $2 \times 10^5$ N/mm$^2$,
determine the stresses developed in each material and the extension of the compound bar when axial tensile force of 60 kN acts.

A steel rail 50 m long is at a temperature of $27^\circ$C. Estimate the elongation when temperature increases to $56^\circ$C. Calculate the thermal stress in the rail if (i) No expansion gap provided (ii) A 7 mm gap is provided for expansion.
